name: Veterinary dental care for pets
summary: How expats arrange professional pet dental cleaning and oral surgery in Singapore — anaesthesia norms, cost ranges, and why “anaesthesia-free dentistry” marketing is a red flag for most dogs and cats.
body:
Pet dental disease is common in condo-living dogs and cats eating mostly kibble. Professional cleaning under anaesthesia lets vets chart, probe, polish, and extract safely — something scale-only “anaesthesia-free” stalls cannot do below the gumline.

## What to expect
- Pre-anaesthetic exam and often bloodwork
- Full-mouth charting, dental radiographs when available
- Scaling, polishing, and extractions as needed
- Pain relief and home-care plans (brushing, diets, chews)
- Follow-up for oral surgery cases

Import-new pets may arrive with deferred dental care from the relocation scramble — book once AVS settling allows elective anaesthesia.

## Cost honesty
Quotes can jump after radiographs reveal root disease. Ask what is included vs variable extractions. Pet insurance often excludes pre-existing dental disease — check waiting periods early.

## How to choose
Prefer AVS-licensed clinics with dental radiography and clear anaesthetic monitoring standards. Be sceptical of anaesthesia-free packages for small dogs with heavy tartar. Ask who monitors anaesthesia and what happens if complications arise.

## Practical tip
Start toothbrush acclimation weeks before the procedure. Fasting instructions matter — confirm exact hours for your pet’s size and species.
